Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates unilateral hyperlucency and hyperinflation of the right lung with a diminished right hilum, which are classic radiographic features of Swyer-James-MacLeod syndrome. This condition is a post-infectious obliterative bronchiolitis that typically follows severe viral pneumonia in early childhood, matching the patient's history of severe pulmonary infection at age two.
